contexts.text: See Candlestick.
The reason oil of olive was employed for the... lamps () was that it represented everything celestial...
The lamps () = celestial things, from which are spiritual things; as from flame... is light.
A lamp () = the light of truth.
The light of a lamp shall not shine () = no intelligence of truth.

Afterwards it was allowed to represent before (the Spirits of Mercury) a very pleasant garden full of lights and lamps; then they stayed... because lights with lamps = Truths which shine from good. SE 1431.
That a lamp = faith, and the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of good, which are from the Lord alone, is evident from the places in the Word... where a lamp is mentioned. AC 9548:5, Illustrated.
The lamp () = the Divine truth which is from the Lord.

It treats here of the extinction of faith and of the derivative intelligence in spiritual things; which are the lamp which shall no longer be, and the light of the lamp which shall be taken away (; ).
Thy Word is a lamp unto my foot (. AC 105).
The lamp of the body is the eye... ().

As faith, and the derivative intelligence and wisdom, are signified by a lamp, the kings of Judah are called the lamps of David (. ); and David is called the lamp of Israel (): not that the kings of Judah were lamps, nor David; but because by a king is signified the Divine truth which is from the Lord; and by David the Lord as to the Divine truth; from which are faith, intelligence, and wisdom.

Thou shalt make the lamps thereof, seven () = the holy spiritual things thence; (for) a lamp = faith and the intelligence of truth, which are from the Lord alone; thus the Spiritual; for the Divine truth which is from the Lord, and through which are faith, intelligence, and wisdom, is the Spiritual... The reason the lamps were seven in number, was that the Divine truth, from which are faith, intelligence, and wisdom, is what is called holy...
The lamp, which is the Lamb, that is, the Lord, = faith, and the derivative intelligence of truth and wisdom of good, which are from the Lord alone.

To cause the lamp to go up constantly () = faith thence, and through faith the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of good from the Lord... The reason a lamp = faith, is that the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord is the light in the Heavens. This light, received by the Angels there, or by man, is like a lamp; for it illuminates all things of the mind, and gives intelligence and wisdom. Light, received, is faith. But it is to be known that faith is not a lamp, nor an illuminator of the mind, unless it is from charity...
A lamp () = the Divine truth from which is intelligence.
A lamp () = the truth and good of faith. References.

In dressing the lamps... () = when truth also comes into its light. Lamps = Divine truth, and the derivative intelligence and wisdom. That to dress or kindle them = when those things come into their light, is evident. AC 10202.
Doctrine as a lamp. (See Doctrine.) AC 10582:3. DSS 52. DSS 54. DSS 59. AE 356:2.
That doctrine made from the Word by one who is illustrated must be as a lamp to the understanding. References.
Their wax serves mankind for candles in the whole world.
Kindle a lamp, and inquire...

There is nothing said about the lamps of these (seven) candlesticks; but in what follows it is said that the Holy Jerusalem, that is, the New Church, has no need of the sun, nor of the moon, because its lamp is the Lamb...; and further, They have no need of a lamp, because the Lord God enlightens them (); for those who will be of the Lord's New Church are only candlesticks, which will shine from the Lord.
The light of a lamp shall not shine in thee any more () = that with those... there is not any enlightenment from the Lord and the derivative perception of spiritual truth.

Because the glory of God hath enlightened it, and its lamp is the Lamb = that the men of that Church... from the Divine truth of the Word are in spiritual light from the Lord alone... Because this enlightenment is from the Lord, it is said, and its lamp is the Lamb.
They have no need of a lamp () = that... in the New Jerusalem men will not be in Knowledges concerning God from natural lumen. Explained.
See Lamp.
The regenerate are like the lamps of the candlestick in the tabernacle.
A miraculous lamp always burning (of the Jesuits there). SE 5417, Explained.
As a candlestick derives its representative from its lamps, and the lamps from the light, which in Heaven is Divine truth, therefore the Lord also is called a lamp. Illustrated.
By a lamp, in general, is signified truth from good and the derivative intelligence.
A lamp () = Divine truth from which is Divine intelligence.
The eye is here called a lamp, or a lamp shining, because the eye = the understanding of truth, and thence also the truth of faith.
That the Lord as to Divine truth proceeding from His Divine good is called a lamp. Reference.
By the fire kindled in the lamps (in the tabernacle) was signified spiritual love, which is love towards the neighbour; in like manner by the oil of olive... of which was the fire.
I will dispose a lamp for Mine Anointed () = the enlightenment of Divine truth from the unition of the Divine and the Human in the Lord; a lamp = Divine truth as to enlightenment.
The eye... is called a lamp, from the light of truth, which man has from understanding and faith.
Unless doctrine is the lamp.
The light of a lamp shall not shine in thee any more = that there is nothing of the truth of Heaven and of the Church... A lamp, or a candlestick, = Heaven and the Church.
